lxc_2f14e24f77d6b02e.text: Science fiction gave us thinking robots, perfect robot laws and machines that grow smarter by themselves.

lxc_93afe6fa720f9e53.text: Real AI in 2026 can hold a fluent conversation, but it predicts words instead of understanding them, its safety rules can be broken, and it cannot improve itself after it is released.

lxc_207682f5880527f6.text: Imagine you are typing messages to two strangers in another room.

lxc_d4ffd088c9b8d924.text: One is a person and one is a machine.

lxc_6c35c7f336f13ea0.text: You can ask anything you like.

lxc_35a9d38b9fc6ceca.text: At the end, you have to guess which one is the machine.

lxc_b11a4fa042e267f3.text: If you can't tell, has the machine won?

lxc_39ce4b5308421d58.text: In the early 1950s, the British mathematician Alan Turing proposed exactly this kind of test.

lxc_93df565b4688c57f.text: A machine answers questions, and it wins if people cannot tell whether it is human or machine.

lxc_590c01305f9a38d2.text: This idea became the basis of the famous Turing Test for machine intelligence.

lxc_f8d5b1198c6bc9dc.text: Notice what the test actually measures.

lxc_ee1967c9dfbc0568.text: It does not look inside the machine.

lxc_9d42023175a5e83e.text: It only asks whether people are convinced.

lxc_818ae30b39600d20.text: So the test is really about imitation, as its name says.

lxc_ab4305805805ef6c.text: This matters, because machines started passing it long before today's AI.

lxc_013ae4cd1956efdf.text: In 2001, a chatbot called A.L.I.C.E. repeatedly convinced people that it was human.

lxc_aca58ad900fa5be4.text: Nobody believes that A.L.I.C.E. was a thinking mind.

lxc_33cafc67b4a655e5.text: It was a program that produced good replies.

lxc_8a7c11d5ebcee34b.text: So the Turing Test tells us something real, but limited.

lxc_bad2954e3265e90f.text: A machine that passes it is very good at seeming human.

lxc_e45f5aa1f471f6a0.text: That is not the same as being a mind.

lxc_377057a51abede68.text: Today's chatbots are far more fluent than A.L.I.C.E.

lxc_909098148832af0b.text: They can write poems, explain science and answer in many languages.

lxc_9d9e354f3964adee.text: So how do they do it?

lxc_b5a08b4f31dabaf6.text: A modern chatbot has learned patterns from huge amounts of text.

lxc_a965bce117d31199.text: When you write a question, it calculates which words and phrases are likely to come next, and then it adds them one after another.

lxc_9bd9fcf8a14fb2f8.text: Think of the autocomplete on your phone, which suggests the next word in a message.

lxc_576ff39b38ba4829.text: A chatbot works like a very powerful version of that, and it continues for whole pages.

lxc_5eda830c88ff7e1c.text: Human writing is full of patterns, so a system that predicts those patterns well will sound natural.

lxc_c8f0cca5eb156161.text: Some experts describe chatbots as "stochastic parrots".

lxc_a32d389ba54f52ad.text: A parrot can repeat words without knowing what they mean.

lxc_d99e0e3e611c81c6.text: In the same way, a chatbot produces likely phrases, but it does not truly understand the content.

lxc_0f01da59a8cb28f3.text: Real systems such as large language models are probabilistic, which means they work with chances, not certainty.

lxc_779f31f3553a5ae2.text: Here the gap between fiction and fact is clear.

lxc_c8d36c2d6ad306da.text: Fictional AI characters often have consciousness.

lxc_d19a823303673ab5.text: They have feelings, goals and an inner life.

lxc_206ed91a45132afd.text: If machines become powerful, how do we keep them safe?

lxc_6188626fc3d508e5.text: The science-fiction writer Isaac Asimov imagined one answer.

lxc_333f7c33ff98be7c.text: His fictional robots were programmed with the Three Laws of Robotics.

lxc_f1ffe85645e834e5.text: These laws made sure the robots would not threaten humans or each other.

lxc_9e089e1e68f7dc7b.text: In the stories, these laws are built deep into every robot.

lxc_6b239215fee14734.text: A robot cannot simply decide to ignore them.

lxc_9844ef02a3f1689f.text: They are absolute, and they are part of how the story world works.

lxc_8f3b730d88cd8815.text: Real AI safety looks very different.

lxc_5dc3d89bcdcae43e.text: One method is to train AI models to refuse harmful requests.

lxc_4c7d6adb4e0e887f.text: Another is to build tools that can detect content made by AI.

lxc_2577b4a7fc95bfaf.text: These are useful steps, but they are not unbreakable laws.

lxc_0634a0e0afa2a340.text: Many safeguards can be bypassed, and their real-world effectiveness is still uncertain.

lxc_1976d8033a1d3ded.text: Why is there such a difference?

lxc_682191cdfce2ba35.text: A chatbot doesn't follow a list of rules the way a robot in a story does.

lxc_7e459a9291b6453b.text: Training can make refusing harmful requests very likely, but a clever user may still find a way around it.

lxc_56017313a66f6d21.text: A trained habit is not a law of nature.

lxc_0745e03cb1f273f2.text: Real AI safety today is more like teaching good habits, and habits can be broken.

lxc_05358c724e6c8508.text: One of the most exciting and frightening ideas in science fiction is a machine that improves itself.

lxc_98609d7f14a89b55.text: It learns, it upgrades its own abilities, and then it uses those new abilities to improve again.

lxc_83f4992d126dfa91.text: In stories, this can lead to a machine that leaves humans far behind.

lxc_af32cee5a963afaf.text: This fear is old and deep in fiction.

lxc_92fee282df2b8124.text: In Frank Herbert's Dune series, for example, there are stories about banning AI and smart machines.

lxc_d13af295b46a5ad0.text: Stories like these reflect society's worries about what AI might become.

lxc_f1eb85dd0c80ada4.text: Researchers take the idea of self-improvement seriously.

lxc_e174236a05858d36.text: They call one part of it continual learning, which means learning and getting better over time.

lxc_f48490b9c8937f77.text: It is considered important for building AGI, a general AI that could match humans across many tasks.

lxc_a7bec51e8b674829.text: But here is the reality check.

lxc_afc53b4d6390b6fb.text: Current AI systems generally do not have their own way to improve themselves after deployment.

lxc_009fcab13c283a93.text: In other words, once a model is released, it doesn't keep upgrading itself.

lxc_0dc272fca383f7f4.text: People still train and update it.

lxc_62de3254af3d6f1a.text: Real self-improvement would require new ideas, but current AI systems have difficulty producing original scientific insights.

lxc_46c66dad652f83a1.text: A machine that cannot easily discover something new cannot easily invent a better version of itself.

lxc_be66ed5192995941.text: So the runaway machine of fiction is not here yet.

lxc_f83c06a7f63917e9.text: The idea is important to researchers, but the key ingredients are missing.

lxc_fe3b518b43bdd1d5.text: Some science fiction goes even further.

lxc_83a13ae8170c10d1.text: In The Matrix, AI robots enslave humans inside a simulated reality.

lxc_397f6f2473136a13.text: The people live their whole lives in a virtual world and believe it is real.

lxc_b1dfac2a24b931a7.text: At first, this seems like the biggest idea of all.

lxc_8b51303b12cbf2c7.text: But look at what makes it frightening.

lxc_9abc984b2e0242c4.text: The machines in The Matrix are dangerous because humans cannot tell what is real.

lxc_a7b307da1c61eaf6.text: Now think back to Turing's Imitation Game from Part 1.

lxc_2c80b10916c68002.text: It asks the same question: can humans tell the difference between the real thing and an imitation?

lxc_21e433ab4b96955e.text: This is exactly where modern chatbots are strong, because they generate human-like text by predicting likely phrases.

lxc_e2fa98b243c7affe.text: A chatbot cannot build a world to trap us.

lxc_7379f3f483ac830c.text: But it can produce human-like text so well that people may forget they are talking to a machine.

lxc_75f06101db331439.text: So the wonder and the warning of science fiction meet in the same place.

lxc_993e59d635fa53ba.text: The most realistic part of these stories is not the thinking robot.

lxc_9725730eb03be437.text: It is the human who is convinced.
